title: Speech and the Tongue
lead: What the Bible says about words: the power of the tongue to give life or to kill, truth and lies, gossip and slander, the wise use of silence, and the gentle answer, from the Law's ban on false witness and talebearing through Proverbs and the Psalms to Jesus and James.

sections.b: The Law protects people from harmful words: it forbids false testimony (Exodus 20:16; Deuteronomy 19:16–19) and going about as a slanderer (Leviticus 19:16). Proverbs gathers more sayings on speech than on any other single subject: the mouth can be "a spring of life" (Proverbs 10:11), a sword or a cure (Proverbs 12:18), and "Death and life are in the tongue's hand" (Proverbs 18:21). The wise speak little and at the right time (Proverbs 10:19; Proverbs 15:23); a soft answer turns anger back (Proverbs 15:1). The Psalms pray for a guard over the mouth (Psalm 141:3). Jesus says people will give account for every careless word (Matthew 12:36–37), and James calls the tongue a small fire that can set a forest ablaze (James 3:1–12). Jewish teaching built on these texts the laws of lashon hara, harmful speech about others.
